📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo has spoken out on making his transfer to Liverpool permanent after his loan spell this season.

The Uruguay international has started brightly with the Reds, instantly settling in well to life in the Premier League and becoming a key player under Andoni Iraola.

Still, it seems Araujo has not yet decided if he’ll be staying at Liverpool beyond the end of this season, as he insists it still depends on a number of factors and decisions made by different people.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

That’s what Araujo told the Athletic in an interview, as they also state that Liverpool have the option to sign him for €55m.

When asked if he’d like to stay at Anfield, the 27-year-old responded: “I think it’s still very early to talk about that. I try to take each day as it comes, enjoy myself and do what I like doing best.

“There’s still a long way to go (in his loan) and it doesn’t depend on just one person; it depends on a lot of people. So we have to wait and, when the time comes, make whatever decision needs to be made.”.

It seems Araujo isn’t ruling out staying with Liverpool, but one imagines he doesn’t want to commit too hard to anything right now, as there’s always a chance Barca will want him back.

In many ways, it’s a little hard to understand why Barcelona let Araujo go, as he’s shown himself to be a really solid and reliable defensive performer for Liverpool.

LFC fans would surely be delighted if he joined permanently, though of course it could also be unwise for the club to make that decision now in case his form dips as the season goes on.

#37185. Breaking: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's vital.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (938 w)
📖 Baca

Breaking: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's vital.

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black?
  • Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?
  • Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes.

Your brain has its own version of that.

Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?

Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.

It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas.

That's your brain's default mode network.

Scientists conducted brain-imaging experiments in the 1990s and early 2000s to find out which regions of the brain were active during demanding tasks, like solving a math problem or memory exercise.

But to measure that, they needed a so-called baseline. They needed to know the level of brain activity at rest and during demanding tasks.

So, between the tasks, they asked participants to relax, close their eyes, stare at a fixed point on a wall, or try not to think of anything at all.

According to recent reports, and they measured the participants' brain activity both when they were solving a task and doing nothing. That's how scientists noticed the brain was active in up- and downtime.

Industry observers note that they noticed that when participants started to focus on a upcoming task, after having done nothing, some brain areas lit up and other areas dimmed down. That suggests those areas that dimmed down must have been active while the participant was apparently — physically and mentally — at rest.

This realization eventually led to the discovery of the default mode network or DMN.

The DMN is crucial because it helps your brain make sense of your life and experiences.

It helps you connect and revisit memories, reflect on who you are, imagine what might happen in future scenarios, understand other people, build meaning from experience, and connect ideas in new ways.

It turns all your memories, experiences, knowledge, emotions and social information into your internal story. Think of that story as a constantly evolving, updated model of who you are and how you engage with the world around you.

It has been revealed that but it's important to understand the DMN involves more than one area of the brain. It is a group of brain regions that light up when you're not focused on an external task.

There's another player in your brain that acts as a monitoring system. You can think of it as constantly asking "Is there anything that needs my attention?".

Imagine you're daydreaming while driving, and a car suddenly swerves into your lane.

Industry observers note that in a fraction of a second, your daydream disappears and your attention snaps back to the road. That player is called the salience network, or SN.

The salience network helps you notice key signals, like a sound, a mistake, pain, an emotion, a threat, or something happening in your body, and helps shift the brain toward attention and control systems when action is needed.

The DMN, SN and attention/control systems constantly interact.

And the DMN doesn't just turn off completely with every hard task. Parts of it can also contribute when tasks involve memory, stories, meaning or other people.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, smartphones have filled many of the small empty moments of our days — waiting for the bus, standing in line, eating alone, lying on the couch. We are constantly looking at our devices.

So, it seems reasonable to ask: are we crowding out those moments of boredom where DMN kicks in?

In a recent development, maybe. But so far, there's no strong evidence that scrolling directly affects mental health by reducing DMN time.

What we do know is that problematic smartphone use can increase stress, anxiety, task-switching and disrupt sleep.

And sleep loss and stress also have clearer evidence for altering DMN-related brain connectivity.

The DMN is not always necessarily good.

When your mind wanders, it might produce a great latest idea.

Recent findings suggest that but it might also replay an embarrassing thing you did five years ago. Again. And again.

In depression, the self-reflection part of the DMN can get caught in repetitive negative loops that are hard to stop — what's known as rumination.

Sources indicate that scientists have also found that Alzheimer's disease targets key DMN areas, particularly those responsible for your autobiographical memory and remembering other aspects of the past. Which may help explain why memory problems are so central to the disease.

Protect your sleep and take stress seriously. There is direct evidence that sleep loss and stress disrupt DMN-related connectivity.

Take real, quiet breaks after mentally demanding tasks, like studying. It can even help you memorize facts for your exam.

Embrace boredom and enjoy doing nothing.

Try to reframe boredom as this essential, energy-intensive active work in your brain that builds your internal narrative and sense of self, consolidates memories, creates connections and sparks creativity.

Try waiting in line without checking your phone. Look out the window next time you take the bus or take a walk without listening to anything.

You can also try scheduling DMN time. It may be the closest thing to a real brain hack.

Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

📅 25 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish.
  • Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make.
  • Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an vital afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that but Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

Recent findings suggest that and how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

According to recent reports, with the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two massive chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an notable moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite promptly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

“The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Sources indicate that brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix.

It has been revealed that iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu.

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

Ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very swiftly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

There will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully launches it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Recent findings suggest that kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

As expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

In a recent development, gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

According to recent reports, brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

Recent findings suggest that once again, Liverpool break through Gakpo. This time, it comes from a Brighton corner, but Gakpo’s cross for Isak at the back post is read by Dunk.

In his first involvement since entering the action, Nyoni ends a slick Brighton move by taking the ball off De Cuyper’s toe in the penalty area with a much-needed clearance. He seems to be limping after he was caught by De Cuyper.

Wirtz’s game is over and he departs to be replaced by Nyoni in Liverpool’s first change.

After some treatment for Wirtz, Vuskovic eventually takes the free kick. It’s in such an inviting position, but the defender gets too power on his strike and whips it over the bar.

It has been revealed that this game is still very much in the balance, even though Liverpool have a two goal advantage, and it speaks volumes about both teams’ commitment to attack. The questions the respective head coaches are asking of their players are relentless but the players are responding by being adventurous in how they attack and where they want to get on the ball. How Andoni Iraola and Fabian Hurzeler deploy their substitutes will be significant.

Liverpool are holding firm, with Brighton yet to create an opportunity in this second half. Ayari is apprehended by Wirtz to win a free kick on the edge of the area. Despite committing the foul, Wirtz has stayed down and is clutching his ankle.

Brighton make another change and it’s a straight swap in midfield as Yalcouye replaces Chema Andres, who hobbles off the pitch.

It has been revealed that with Brighton requiring at least two goals to avoid defeat, they’ll need to push a lot of men forward, which will open up space for Liverpool to exploit on the break. If there is one, the next goal in this game is crucial.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool break through Gakpo, who sprints from inside his own half into the penalty. He tries to release Isak, but his pass is intercepted by Vuskovic as he’s swarmed by the Brighton defence. Gakpo waited too long and should have played the pass earlier.

In a recent development, kerkez isn’t switched on and fails to deal with a long ball, allowing Gomez to race in behind. Van Dijk covers Kerkez and blocks Gomez’s pass, with Kostoulas sprinting up in support.

Sources indicate that we are back under way for the second half. Hurzeler has made one half-time alteration, with Hinshelwood replacing Boscagli, who was booked just before the break. Meanwhile, Liverpool are unchanged as they look to protect their two-goal advantage.

Wirtz’s wickedly deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s neat finish from close range mean Liverpool are two goals in front against Brighton. The visitors have also looked dangerous going forward, with Ayari wasting a golden chance when the score was still goalless, before hitting the post in the 36th minute. As it stands, this result would move Liverpool into fourth and a point behind Brighton, who need a massive second-half performance.

Two goals to the good for @LFC 😮‍💨 A Pascal Gross own goal puts the Reds ahead, before Alexander Isak fires in the second 🔴 https://t.co/AglQOyUIoY.

In a recent development, brighton are desperate to find a goal before the break as Kostoulas’ fierce shot is batted away by Alisson, whose goal is living a charmed life. Boscagli then receives a yellow card for blocking Barcola’s off-the-ball run.

No getting away from the fact that Brighton simply haven’t got started and it’s a huge surprise. What chances they have had came from Liverpool’s own shortcomings and it is impossible to think they will be so off the pace in the second period. Fabian Hurzeler has remained composed, which is more than can be remarked for Oliver Boscagli, who looks like he is playing pass the parcel, so anxious is he to get rid of the ball - often with a mistake.

On the counter, Gomez tries to find Ayari with a pass, but Jacquet’s touch knocks the ball out of Liverpool’s box. There will be three minutes of added time to end this half.

Araujo forces a save as he sprints forward from his right-back position to receive a clipped pass from Mac Allister, before shooting from a tight angle to sting the palms of Verbruggen with a drilled effort.

Gakpo drives at Brighton’s defence and then nearly squeezes a low cross to the supporting Isak, but Dunk’s crucial intervention with his outstretched leg prevents a chance.

Off the post for Brighton. Ayari shoots from an incredibly long way out as Brighton dispossess Mac Allister and Jacquet, however his curling effort agonisingly bounces against the post and out, with Alisson well beaten.

Manchester City fans have lost their patience with one star player after they put in a 'terrible' performance during a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham on Saturday afternoon.

The Cityzens have now gone four Premier League matches in a row without a win - a worrying change of fortune after having started the 26/27 season with a 100 per cent record in the six previous fixtures.

In a recent development, maresca's side were forced to fight hard for a point in the lunchtime kick-off, having gone a goal down after 16 minutes courtesy of Rodrigo Muniz's opener. While Erling Haaland's goal 10 minutes later was controversially ruled out, it took a brilliant volley from Elliot Anderson in the second-half to rescue a draw.

It is clear that off-field problems are denting confidence during their current run, but some of the Etihad faithful are starting to point their finger at particular players, who have struggled to continue the good times rolling after Pep Guardiola's departure at the end of the last campaign.

After picking up just one point at home this weekend, some City fans are now turning on Phil Foden, who has been at the club since he joined the academy at eight-years-old.

Sources indicate that writing on X, many supporters slammed his lack of influence in attack, while paying close attention to his reluctance to press when out of possession. One user remarked:.

"I’ve said this a dozen times. Phil Foden is done playing football. He has nothing left to offer. He is just finished.".

A second wrote: "This Foden guy man, I lost my patience, 9 years and still a project player, zero qualities that require to start him," as a third continued: "Can always count on Foden to have zero impact as a 10.".

Elsewhere, a fourth brutally asked: "What's the point in giving Foden even one minute of playing time?" as a fifth concluded: "Foden, it’s all well and good to ask for the ball and touch it a thousand times, but if you’re just going to play it backwards or create nothing, my guy, get off the pitch.".

It remains difficult to say whether City's current struggles are down to the ongoing uncertainty surrounding their 115 charges, or whether Maresca's honeymoon period at the Etihad is coming to a swift end.

Many will also argue that the Italian is getting his attacking selections wrong at the moment, with the likes of Rayan Cherki and Enzo Fernandez among those left on the bench.

Whatever the underlying matter, the Cityzens now have a mountain to climb if they are to have any chance of toppling Arsenal at the top of the table.

The Gunners have the opportunity to move eight points clear of their usual title rivals if they beat Newcastle on Saturday evening, although Brighton could still cut that gap to five points should the Seagulls pick up a win themselves.

But let’s momentarily keep to that bizarre video, which has been watched almost two million times on Gabriel’s Instagram page, and from there we can raise the question of whoever thought it was a good idea.

This is where we should introduce Ali Barat, the owner of Epic Sports. He’s a big fish in the world of football agencies and the 31-second clip was advertising their latest coup: Gabriel had joined his group, which is timely because a move to Real is imminent and that will follow other big deals brokered by Barat.

According to recent reports, they include Moises Caicedo to Chelsea for £115million, Noni Madueke to Arsenal for £52m and Dean Huijsen to Bournemouth for £12.6m, then on to Real Madrid for £50m more. He’s a significant figure with a changeable definition of what it means to be understated. Here’s an example from his company’s website: ‘While some agents seek the spotlight, Ali Barat is quietly reshaping the transfer market.’.

Amusingly, it then goes on to describe Barat as a ‘super-agent’ twice in the same paragraph while declaring he is ‘not just closing deals, he is building careers, guiding legacies, and setting the standard for a new era of football representation’.

Industry observers note that the ‘quiet’ part was possibly lost along the way. But ‘legacy’ is the word among that salad most worthy of fixation, because Gabriel has been steered to a series of pivotal decisions at an incredibly young age.

He is yet to play a single minute of competitive senior football but he is clear on what he wishes to become. Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel said: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or.’.

Fair enough. He’s a teenager aiming high. Is it wise to say so? Maybe not, but he’s 16. Barat, the super-agent, has no such excuse. He’s 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid.

It has been revealed that there’s less ambiguity in the wisdom of what Barat has done there. It reeks. It carries the stench of an agent who evidently doesn’t mind so much if the labels attached to Gabriel today stick for the remainder of his career.

Welsh Rugby Union's 20,000 reasons to be ashamed.

Among the joys of this job is being present at rare moments of sporting greatness. The Welsh win over the All Blacks last weekend was one such occasion and, for me, it was compounded by a subsequent email from a lovely chap named John Evans, aged 87 and from Tredegar in Blaenau Gwent.

John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten New Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

After detailing how he, ‘a small-bottomed outside-half’, had left himself with no view of the pitch at the back of the stand, John went on to recall that the crowd around him and a friend ‘decided to pass us over everyone’s head back down to the front’. He landed just in time to see Ken Jones score the winning try. His excitement in sharing a memory from 73 years ago was spelled out in block capitals.

One of the consequences of the ongoing shambles at the Welsh Rugby Union is that there were 20,000 empty seats at the Principality Stadium last weekend, mainly due to a combination of apathy and protest. Accordingly, there will be 20,000 fewer people with a great story to tell decades from now. While the WRU ponder their next blunders, they might wish to consider some of the above.

Breaking: How to make AI data centres more sustainable

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1295 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • Industry observers note that is the climate totally cooked?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

In a recent development, around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Industry observers note that is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

It has been revealed that people have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

Future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

The Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres right now consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency states.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Recent findings suggest that there are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

But none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that fresh energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

Many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of new energy needed to power data centres.

According to recent reports, how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

In a recent development, how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

Recent findings suggest that one solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any newly introduced generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

There is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a strategy for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI announced what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the firm can work around peaks in power demand.

Meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

These are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any latest energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

There are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

#37176. Bundesliga treat Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or as beacon of hope as Germany's competitiveness questions linger

Bundesliga treat Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or as beacon of hope as Germany's competitiveness questions linger

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2120 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even if the hints of a smile never fully leave his face, there is an overriding sense of practicality when Philipp Lahm speaks.
  • Recent findings suggest that "It helped Harry Kane and Michael Olise that they came from another country," Lahm mentioned four days after Kane's major win.
  • In a recent development, A quick glance at the data would confirm the hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even if the hints of a smile never fully leave his face, there is an overriding sense of practicality when Philipp Lahm speaks. He seems to have shed the intensity associated with the life of a professional athlete nearly a decade after retiring, but the characteristics of a World Cup-winning captain are hard to miss. He is friendly and open but also serious, so when the topic of conversation shifts to Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, he is politely unflinching in his assessment of what the award means for soccer in Germany.

Recent findings suggest that "It helped Harry Kane and Michael Olise that they came from another country," Lahm mentioned four days after Kane's major win. "I think it's quite difficult for a German player playing in the Bundesliga [to win the Ballon d'Or].".

In a recent development, A quick glance at the data would confirm the hypothesis. The last Bundesliga-based player and the last German player to win the sport's most prestigious individual award was Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer in 1996. A German player has only finished inside the top three of the Ballon d'Or three times since, the last being Manuel Neuer in 2014, while Kane is only the seventh Bundesliga player to rank in the top three since Sammer's win. Lahm seamlessly links the pattern to another less-than-ideal trend in Germany's top flight -- Bayern Munich, with whom he won eight Bundesliga titles, are the division's indisputable kings.

In a recent development, they have lost the title just once since the 2012-13 season, a lack of competitiveness at the top of the table a natural consequence of their dominance. This is, in some ways, not Bayern's problem, but a narrative persists in Germany regardless. Players have historically been unable to reach the peaks of the game in Germany because of the circumstances, inspiring a wide-ranging set of side effects. Kane's move to Bayern was not designed to be anything other than the right move at the right time for a player talented enough to compete for the UEFA Champions League, but three years later, those invested in the Bundesliga's success are beginning to treat him as a beacon of hope.

"I do hope that the good players stay in the Bundesliga," Lahm mentioned, "so I'm hopeful through Harry Kane that a lot of other players will follow because it's possible to win and play here.".

In a recent development, the argument to join Bayern Munich is a straightforward one, if you ask sporting director Christoph Freund -- "you can win titles with us," both in Germany and Europe. Bayern have won the Champions League twice in the last 14 years, a feat matched only by Paris Saint-Germain and topped by Real Madrid. The Bundesliga's distribution of wealth favors them in this case, to the point that it likely played a sizable role in signing Kane and Olise. The balance of financial power in the European club game, though, has shifted as Bayern re-established their foothold in Germany -- the Premier League has become the sport's league of choice because it has the financial might to back up the claim. Players like Robert Lewandowski and Mario Gotze used to prove their worth at other German clubs (and in their specific case, Borussia Dortmund) before climbing up the food chain and joining Bayern. Florian Wirtz's jump from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool in 2025, though, is an example of a latest world order, one some hope Kane's Ballon d'Or might change.

"It's all about the attention, so when you're successful with the German national team that's visible, but then when you play also successful soccer with Liverpool, then the attention in U.K. is much bigger," Lahm mentioned, citing Wirtz's hypothetical Ballon d'Or case as an example, "so that would be more difficult for a German player in the Bundesliga alone, rather than changing to somewhere else outside and being successful abroad.".

Industry observers note that the Bundesliga's international appeal has not only taken a hit on the sporting side in recent years. Bayern's executives believe their club makes up around 50% of the league's brand value globally, and though they are unapologetic about their strengths on the pitch, they also argue they are doing too much of the heavy lifting. Rouven Kasper, a member of Bayern's executive board, pointed to Premier League clubs' oversized presence on preseason tours as a primary example for the Bundesliga to follow but all but questioned the league's interest in the strategy.

"The league needs to be, as well, stronger and bring more reach, but the league exists from the clubs," Kasper remarked. "We are the spearhead of German football, and I think together with the other clubs and together with the league, we need to be even more active in the markets ... it's not enough, and at the end, it's about people, community. We want to be approachable. We want to talk to the people. We want to be there, as the Bundesliga and Bayern alone cannot do it together with Dortmund, so we need more activities from the league and being in different markets, as the U.K. guys are doing and also the Spanish guys are doing. We will do our part.".

Their part includes potentially using Kane as a hook for player recruitment, even if other leagues have their charms for the world's top talents.

Industry observers note that "I think everybody knows the Premier League is the biggest league at the moment," Freund remarked. "Also, Spain is really attractive with Real Madrid and Barcelona, but we know we are Bayern Munich and the German Bundesliga is also really a strong league, a really good league, outstanding stadiums, outstanding atmosphere, and you can [perform] also on a very high level like Harry, the next step in his career, and therefore, I think Bayern Munich and also the German Bundesliga is very attractive, also, for international top players.".

Sources indicate that some in the Bundesliga, though, are resigned to the fact that there are certain things Bayern -- and other European clubs -- will simply beat them to. Dortmund have held strong in their attempts to mount a title challenge this season, level on points with Bayern after eight games thanks to Saturday's 2-2 draw in Der Klassiker. For the foreseeable future, though, recruitment of elite talents cannot and will not play a central role in their quest to win silverware. "We never refuse, or we never avoid to tell you guys where we are from, but in comparison to Munich, Madrid, London, Paris, Milan, we are from Dortmund and from a purely economic perspective, we are far behind them," Borussia Dortmund CEO Carsten Cramer stated. "If they [are] just interested in trophies and silver, if they look for the Ballon d'Or player wearing a black and yellow shirt, maybe that is something we can't offer to them.".

While Bayern's brand is wrapped in the quiet luxury of their domestic stronghold, Cramer argued that Dortmund's appeal is a qualitative one.

"In the last 13 years, we didn't become champion but though we didn't become champion, the interest in Dortmund is still increasing and the amount of people following our club on social media and wherever we travel in the world is quite huge," he said. "We are able to offer a different approach: closeness. That is the Dortmund way, and I think that is maybe one of the reasons that many, many hardcore supporters of one club do have a sympathy for us as a second-love club, which I do not complain about, and that is our way. I don't want to make us too small by saying we are a niche club, but we are for sure a bit different, and I don't complain about [it].".

Patrick Owomoyela, a defender for Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund team that won back-to-back Bundesliga titles more than a decade ago, can clearly map out the recipe to beat Bayern to the top. Strong squad composition and compatibility go a long way, and he believes the current iteration of Dortmund has that -- he praised head coach Niko Kovac's defensive structure and commended him for "sprinkling the creativity" into the team in the months since taking the job in January 2025. There is just one problem, though.

Industry observers note that "Even though you know the recipe, the soup is not always the same," he said. "Even though you put in the same ingredients, it's not always tasting the same, and if it does, maybe it's not the perfect soup, you know? So you need to find that special something.".

Much like Cramer, Owomoyela has a qualitative argument of his own to make when it comes to breaking Bayern's decades-long dominance in the Bundesliga. The "special something" for his Dortmund team was a sense of camaraderie, the foundation of which was Klopp's joyous approach, though he openly admitted that is a difficult thing to replicate.

It has been revealed that "This is sometimes the mentality of the guys or the personality of the guys and how that fits together, on top of the stuff that they can do with the ball and as I said, we weren't the best in terms of playing football," he said. "We were the best team. We had the most fun. We really liked doing a lot of stuff together. We were like a family, and you don't find that all the time, and it gets harder, I would say, every year because football has changed. The looks of players nowadays are totally different ... These guys have a strategy, so they want to be part of something for this period of time, but then they want to move on, and that makes it, of course, hard to find that chemistry because he is gone next year.".

According to recent reports, it is the issue he identified with Leverkusen, the Bundesliga's last champion not named Bayern. Their rise up the ranks in the 2023-24 season was ambitious and impressive, but two years later, the mainstays of their title-winning campaign were elsewhere. Wirtz left for Liverpool, as did Jeremie Frimpong, Granit Xhaka now finds himself at Sunderland, Piero Hincapie now plays for Arsenal and then-head coach Xabi Alonso made a stop at Real Madrid before landing at his current post at Chelsea. Jonathan Tah, meanwhile, went the old-school route and now plays at Bayern. The next challenger to Bayern's throne will likely face the same fate for the foreseeable future, no matter whether its stars move to Munich or settle in England.

Saturday's draw between Bayern and Dortmund, though, has offered a flicker of optimism that the Bundesliga might have a title race on its hands before the next great team gets stripped for parts. The 2-2 scoreline flatters Dortmund -- Bayern racked up 4.48 expected goals and were unlucky when the crossbar denied them on both Kane's second-half penalty and a late strike from Lennart Karl, while the visitors generated just 0.74 xG. Owomoyela argued, though, that Bayern have their flaws.

It has been revealed that "What's it gonna take to take that away from Bayern after all these years again?" he asked. "It's just to believe that it's possible and I think the Bayern team indicated in this season as well, or especially maybe, that you can wound them, you can hurt them and something is possible. You can see that in almost every game they played, even in that cup game [against second-division side Magdeburg on Oct. 28] that they just had and they won it 6-1 ... They hit the post, hit the crossbar, scored a goal, had two other major chances so now take a team with more quality, with the right kind of belief, there might be something possible.".

In a recent development, saturday's Klassiker only added to the Bundesliga's week of good news, presenting a different case of the league's strengths than Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, one that will likely take precedence in the short term. The longer Dortmund keep pace with Bayern, the more intriguing the Bundesliga becomes, and at this stage of the season, the possibility of a genuine title race is easy enough to dream up. That sense of optimism, though, tends to give way to the league's current realities. Even if Dortmund answered the question in the affirmative once, there's a long way to go until anyone can definitively say that Bayern can be topped.

"We weren't really eye-level competitors," Owomoyela stated about Dortmund's ability to compete with Bayern in the years since their back-to-back Bundesliga titles. "We were there and we were able to hunt, but from a little distance, and I think everybody understands that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toni Kroos named an English footballing legend as one of the five best central midfielders in history on a star-studded list of the former Real Madrid midfielder's teammates and rivals.

In a recent development, since Kroos retired in May 2024, he's turned to podcasting and has been making some interesting and controversial assessments of modern-day football. Take, for example, his opinion that Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe didn't deserve to win the Ballon d'Or because of having 'average' seasons outside the World Cup campaign.

Kroos' comments always hold weight though, because of his incredible career, helping Madrid win five Champions League trophies, including three-in-a-row. The German also won the World Cup in 2014 and played in an era with many of football's most celebrated central midfield talents.

When ranking the five best central midfielders in history, "Einfach mal Luppen" podcast in October, Kroos only named one player who is playing today.

Kroos displayed his national allegiance by placing former Chelsea midfielder Michael Ballack in fifth place. The iconic German became a fan favourite during four seasons at Stamford Bridge, playing with grit and determination required of a Premier League midfield icon.

In a recent development, with an extraordinary engine room came a box-to-box midfielder who dominated opponents physically, posed a real aerial threat and knew when to time his runs to perfection. He commanded the respect of his teammates with his passionate personality and that helped him enjoy huge success for club and country.

In December 2021, Kroos went as far as to name Ballack as the best ambidextrous player in history, above Cristiano Ronaldo. He remarked via Sky Sport Germany:.

"Michael Ballack was already outstandingly two-footed. He would have scored far fewer goals if he only had a right foot.".

In a recent development, there are some similarities between Kroos and Steven Gerrard that were hard to ignore during their playing days. Particularly their ability to control games with ease, orchestrating not just the midfield but the entire team thanks to their all-rounded powers.

Gerrard cemented his legacy as a Liverpool hero during his illustrious career at Anfield, a talisman throughout the Merseyside outfit's highs and lows during the 2000s and early 2010s. He captained the Reds to the Champions League trophy in the Miracle of Instanbul in 2005 and his exploits in the FA Cup final win over West Ham United a year later were a sight to behold.

It has been revealed that kroos appeared to strictly be ranking Gerrard based on playing in central midfield because he offered a different opinion when weighing in on the Gerrard, Frank Lampard or Paul Scholes debate. He responded to a fan in 2017 and said that Scholes was the best of those three.

Recent findings suggest that when Kroos truly hit his peak along with Luka Modric and Casemiro as Europe's top midfield three in the mid 2010s, they took over from a Barcelona trio. Among that Catalan trident was Xavi, a masterful Spanish midfield maestro who played a crucial role for the Blaugrana during Pep Guardiola's reign.

It has been revealed that xavi dictated the tempo, dropped deep and moved into pockets and possessed remarkable vision with a phenomenal passing range to boot. With Busquets sitting in defensive midfield, Xavi and Iniesta were able to perform magic and give the opposition all sorts of problems in the middle of the park.

Kroos suggested that he looked up to Xavi and believed players like himself were inspired by the Spaniard (via BolaVIP):.

"Many players of my generation who learned in that position were guided by him and his game. He is an example in many respects, including personally.".

Speaking of the Barcelona trio in whom Kroos' Real Madrid midfield succeeded at the top of European football, the German rated Andres Iniesta even higher. A press-resistent midfield gem whose understanding of the tiki-taka system made him one of the most difficult players to defend against.

Recent findings suggest that iniesta wrote his name in the history books when he scored the winner for Spain in a 1-0 win over the Netherlands in the 2010 World Cup final. His game was more about playmaking than scoring, but that was just one of many trophy-winning goals he netted.

In an interview with Merkur in 2011, Kroos made clear his admiration for both Xavi and Iniesta:.

"When you look at Barcelona's Xavi and Andrés Iniesta in that position – that is simply world-class.".

According to recent reports, topping Kroos' list is his longtime teammate and close friend Luka Modric, who is the only player in this ranking that has won the Ballon d'Or. The Croat broke Ronaldo and Messi's stranglehold on the award by claiming it in 2018 after his instrumental role in Real Madrid's Champions League win and Croatia's unlikely runners-up finish at the World Cup.

Modric at the age of 41, is still playing and rolling back the years at AC Milan, but it was his time with Kroos and Casemiro at the Santiago Bernabeu that truly saw him ascend to the top of the sport. Whether it be finding his man with an inch-perfect 30-yard pass or finding the bottom corner of the net from as many yards, his influence on his teams is undeniable.

After Modric left Madrid but opted not to retire like Kroos, his former teammate explained why he'd shine at the San Siro:.

"He has always been a special player. He will never lose his qualities with the ball.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he remarked, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

Industry observers note that A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by Latest Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres remarked the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach.".

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, mentioned that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he mentioned, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "upcoming era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including significant polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

Financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

Erdogan noted while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest.".

"Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she said, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

Sources indicate that most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, noted the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and quickly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over.".

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," stated Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

"We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine mentioned.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Albanese mentioned it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most.".

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she said, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres remarked, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

Sources indicate that von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands noted electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Recent findings suggest that iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian noted his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the issue to climate finance and said his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms.".

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, said the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he stated.

According to recent reports, he also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he stated.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has hinted he’ll be back by the end of the season after admitting he’s “very disappointed” to have suffered a serious injury.

The England international has been in the form of his life recently, and was rewarded for his efforts with this year’s Ballon d’Or prize, though he’s now set to miss a large chunk of the rest of the campaign.

According to BBC Sport, Kane has already undergone successful surgery on an ankle ligament problem, and it looks set to keep him out for a few months.

As quoted in the report, Kane himself has also hinted at his return date, saying he should be back in time for the business end of the campaign.

“The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027,” Kane said.

The 33-year-old added that he would be “back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season”.

This is a big blow for Bayern and for England, though the next round of internationals aren’t until March, so it’s possible that the former Tottenham striker will be back fit again to feature in those games.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Kane has ten goals in 16 games so far this season for Bayern, following his stunning campaign last year in which he hit 61 goals in 51 appearances in total.

He also recently became the all-time record appearance maker for the England national team, and it feels hugely unfortunate for him to pick up such a lengthy injury while he’s been playing some of his best football.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.
  • After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

This was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Industry observers note that trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Recent findings suggest that trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

Robin Roefs is at it again with another vital save for Sunderland 👏 https://t.co/SJ4qWmSHBo.

Recent findings suggest that had the former Newcastle United player scored so late in the game, the home crowd’s frustration may have boiled over. The point means Le Bris’ side have still not won a league game since August and remain bottom of the table. This is proving to be a tougher second season in the top flight for Sunderland, but if they keep playing like this, they will not remain in the bottom three for much longer.

Industry observers note that “It’s a positive [point],” said Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”.

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it’s a new challenge for us and we need to embrace it. I think we demonstrated this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today.”.

“I think it was a good effort from everybody so obviously we want three points from where we are in the table but keep putting up the performances like that and we’ll get some.

“As a defender it’s always nice to have a clean sheet and especially after the last few games where we haven’t had one.

According to recent reports, “It’s always something we’re looking to do and Robin [Roefs] came up with some big saves, Omar [Alderete] coming on was really good as well and I hope my teammate’s [Nordi Mukiele] OK as well because I think that was kind of my fault. But we got the clean sheet for him so hopefully not too bad.”.

When asked about Sunderland being bottom of the league, he replied: “I think always the table reflects fairly where teams deserve to be, and I think over the course of the course of the season if we keep putting in performances like that it will represent where we should be.

“But the table always reflects where people should be but we need to keep looking at ourselves, don’t look at other anyone else, it’s no-one else’s fault but us and we know that.”.

That result means that Sunderland’s stay bottom of the Premier League and without a win in the competition since August 30, while Leeds earn their fifth draw in eight top-flight fixtures to move up to seventh on 11 points.

The patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point. Players pack their suitcases, board planes, spend a small stretch of days with their compatriots … and in the U.S. men's national team's case, answer questions about their coach landing a new job.

Industry observers note that from the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many. It was not just because job security is an increasingly unrealistic concept for soccer coaches, nor was it only down to the fact that Pochettino initially signed a deal that would expire 22 months later. The last two years have been full of reminders that the USMNT job is one of several that could be available to him – he has openly talked about wanting to return to the Premier League, did not deny that his representatives may have met with AC Milan in the weeks before the World Cup and regularly talks about his undying love for Tottenham Hotspur. The latest iteration of a years-long pattern came Tuesday, when reports out of England suggested Pochettino was a top contender for the Manchester United gig, which is not vacant yet but will be once the club finally parts ways with Michael Carrick.

The cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere. At this stage of Pochettino's tenure with the U.S. team, though, it would be difficult to characterize it as a surprise. It would be equally hard to argue that the pattern does not come with the territory, defender Antonee Robinson acknowledging as much hours after the news broke.

"That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," he said. "Similar things happened in the past, happened at the World Cup where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates and for us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky to work with a top-level manager but it never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp.".

It has been revealed that pochettino's wantaway pattern may be annoying but it reflects the overarching sentiment of his tenure with the USMNT thus far. He is easily the highest-profile coach to take the job and U.S. Soccer is well aware of that. It is why they lined up donors to secure his signature two years ago to make him the federation's highest-paid coach ever, and why there is reportedly a $10 million buyout clause in the newly introduced deal he signed after the World Cup. For the first time in the program's modern history, they hired a coach with genuine international appeal. Even if Robinson should instead spend his time talking about the upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, the fact that Pochettino would be courted by others was baked into his appeal.

In a recent development, "Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and team join," U.S. Soccer CEO J.T. Batson noted in May as chatter around the Milan job took center stage in the early days of the USMNT's World Cup preparations. "He had standing offers from other places to come. He wanted to be here. He's a substantial believer in what we're doing at U.S. Soccer. He's a big believer in soccer in America and he's a big believer in this men's team and so, throughout this entire process, when you have top-class talent, whether it's salespeople, whether it's marketing people or whether it's coaches, other organizations want them and throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent. They've been great partners and are, of course, excited about the summer … There's been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported and so they've been great about that.".

Industry observers note that the key difference here is that he reportedly might be interested in United's offer, according to the Guardian, but the situation remains the same, despite the timing being strange, three months after agreeing a four-year deal. If Pochettino does not end up on United's touchline, his time with the USMNT was never destined to last forever, and U.S. Soccer admitted to it months ago.

It has been revealed that "We actually, on a monthly basis, have a succession planning session for all of our coaches across all of our teams and so as a part of that, we have looks for renewals," Batson mentioned on that May day. "We have plans for interims and we have plans for replacements because you never know what's going to happen. It's a global sport, lots going on and so that's a standard part of us growing up as U.S. Soccer.".

Many might spend the subsequent weeks after Pochettino's hypothetical departure questioning Batson's claim that the Argentine is actually a "significant believer in soccer in America," though the argument is irrelevant as far as the USMNT goes. Pochettino's hire, along with that of U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes a year earlier, was a large statement of intent from U.S. Soccer's leaders like Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, who are relatively fresh to their jobs. Pochettino's exit, therefore, would raise the question of how they continue that vision two years later, especially after outlining an ambitious path for the men's program in the coming years.

Industry observers note that high-profile candidates like Pochettino are not exactly easy to come by, as the initial effort to hire him demonstrated. Ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is easily the most notable name on the market but it is entirely unclear what his next coaching move might be, even if that should not discourage U.S. Soccer from reaching out if they have a vacancy. The options thin out from there if they are only to be measured on their flair, though, making it hard to envision a perfect follow-up act to Pochettino in the short term.

There is a theory that U.S. Soccer may be resigned to picking from a locally sourced talent pool, something that is reinforced by a suggestion that Pochettino was a false steward of American soccer. His departure, if it comes in the short term, is not actually an indictment on U.S. Soccer's approach, nor should it encourage the federation to go for the safest pick next. Pochettino's tenure, at least up until this point, has been an example in reaping rewards for a bold strategy, one that should continue long after he is gone.

In a recent development, pochettino's time with the USMNT has so far been characterized by mixed results, including some low lows that he bears just as much responsibility for as his players. It is not hard to see why he was a good fit for the job, though, and it is not because he makes headlines – his high-intensity, attack-minded style of play actually suited the player pool. The fact that he has coached in a UEFA Champions League final and won a Ligue 1 title with Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar may help with player buy-in, but it would not have papered over the cracks if his version of the USMNT was not actually a decent marriage between his tactical preferences and the players' natural skillsets.

According to recent reports, he continues to feel like a good fit in the post-World Cup months, especially as he oversees a generational shift in the player pool. Pochettino's tenure at Spurs, where he initially made a name for himself as a coach, was defined by his trust in young players but as it pertains to the USMNT's up-and-comers specifically, they already seem well-positioned to slot into his tactical set-up. The team's next great prospects are almost all exclusively attackers; Neil Pierre, the Philadelphia Union 19-year-old in the midst of a breakout season, is so far one of the few notable exceptions at center back.

It has been revealed that A quote-unquote substantial name might not be a realistic option for the USMNT if Pochettino leaves now, though he may have theoretically made the gig more attractive to prospective coaches. More importantly, though, U.S. Soccer is now well-positioned to make a hire based on style and specifically an entertaining and effective style that captured the attention of an otherwise uninterested nation during the World Cup. Straying from that, no matter if Pochettino's successor is world renowned or otherwise, would not match the potential of the USMNT's rising stars, nor would it align with U.S. Soccer's own vision.

Industry observers note that “He is pretty energetic in tight spaces, as he can find his way out of trouble. You might assume his physical strength was a greater priority, but recently he has shown an improvement in his practicality. He can handle duels well.”.
