“We spoke as soon as that quote emerged, but I don’t think he was alluding to the possibility of leaving, it was just a general look at all players. I have a great rapport with him, when he returned to Turin, he immediately came to speak with me, and everything is fine.”.

Although the results did begin to improve towards the break for international duty, the reports continue to swirl that Spalletti’s position on the Juventus bench is not safe.

The situation was not helped by Antonio Conte and France boss Zinedine Zidane confessing they coveted his job.

“I find it absolutely normal that a free agent like Conte should want to sit on an key bench like Italy, Milan, Manchester United or Juventus, so I really don’t understand the reason for all this noise,” shrugged Spalletti.

“When I was between jobs, I would go to watch games and training sessions to learn new things, I studied to find solutions for my next role. I did it with total respect for my present and future, then waited for the right moment to return.”.

There is certainly a long career behind him, as tomorrow will be the 600th Serie A match in his career.

Industry observers note that “I am preparing with the same emotion as I did for my first in Serie A. There were moments during this journey that marked my career as a coach. I’m very happy to have had this tour in football, because it was my life and what I always wished for.

“I learned to be happy even when things are not going in my favour, and I hope to keep going for as long as possible.”.

Juventus missed out on Champions League football last season and run the genuine risk of doing it again this term after a rough start, so do they have time to catch up?

“I do think we have that possibility, but our objective is to become something,” replied the coach.

“If we do that, then we can get good results and a strong position in the table. We have to rely on our work, we want to create habits for constant improvement.”.

Among the worst experiences of his coaching career was Venezia, when Spalletti was fired twice in one season.

Sources indicate that “I have fond memories of a melancholic but splendid city. Those were my first seasons, I had strong Presidential and directorial figures, the team was struggling, so I was fired, and brought back.

Industry observers note that “I want to congratulate Davide Nicola, as wherever he goes in his career, he brings a solution to problems and fuels enthusiasm. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya said.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud.".

Industry observers note that mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager said in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

The youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

In a recent development, as a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

"He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

"Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Recent findings suggest that borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

According to recent reports, at the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

Even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

Industry observers note that with Gladbach at the moment in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

Industry observers note that the 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself notes he doesn't even know how much he's presently earning at Gladbach.

It has been revealed that "My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me.".

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp stated with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either.".

Sources indicate that since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open, even if he does play for Germany. According to FIFA regulations, players under the age of 21 can change national teams before their fourth international match (whether a competitive or friendly match), provided that none of those matches take place during a World Cup or a continental tournament such as the European Championship, Copa America, or Africa Cup of Nations.

Sources indicate that if Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

#37161. What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2587 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it couldn't happen, could it?
  • The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September.
  • According to recent reports, that is why Michael Carrick had to go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it couldn't happen, could it? The answer to that is probably not but the fact that, after Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Manchester United being relegated to the Championship is a prospect that can be discussed as anything other than rival fan fiction ought to terrify the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

A quarter of the season is gone. The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September. You'll struggle to find many teams who can sincerely argue they've been mistreated by the fixture list and United are certainly not one of them. They are where they are, 18th, a point behind Coventry City and safety, and there is not much to explain that away.

According to recent reports, that is why Michael Carrick had to go. On Wednesday morning, the 45-year-old was still taking training at the club's Carrington base but he is expected to be relieved of his duties once the United hierarchy have met in Monaco. There, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to tell minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that it is time to part ways with Carrick. Meanwhile, talks have already begun for USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino to take the helm, returning to the Premier League two and a half years after leaving Chelsea and mere months after signing a upcoming deal with US Soccer. It would appear that unfinished business in England -- and the Old Trafford vacancy to which he has been linked for so long -- has tempted the Argentine away on the eve of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals.

Recent findings suggest that the path Pochettino is now on is one fraught with risk. And yet coaching for survival and nothing else would be the latest in a line of clumsy decisions from the Old Trafford hierarchy. Projection models such as Opta's would probably make the case that this team is dicing with danger but, with a 22% chance of relegation, will probably be fine. Bookmakers too are pretty skeptical that United's 2027-28 will encompass trips to Blackburn and Millwall with eight or so teams priced as more likely to go down than the Red Devils. That will be informed by an analytics profile that really does not suggest United are one of the three worst teams in the Premier League.

Through 10 games, a sample size where expected goals (xG) is more predictive than goals and scorelines when it comes to future results, United have an xG difference of -0.27. If there is an average team in the division, it's Carrick's. Naturally, that is not good enough for a team with their aspirations. Another 28 games putting up those underlying numbers and United will live to fight another day.

Industry observers note that suppose they don't. As anyone that saw Sunday's game can attest, events with a significantly less than 22% probability can happen all the time. A team's xG profile doesn't always capture everything. If it did, Villa would have notably fewer than their 13 points. Things could go worse for United. Let's have a look at how that might happen.

In a recent development, carrick departs Old Trafford with his reputation among the fanbase still intact. He might also find that future employers look more forgivingly on his time at United. His tally of 47 points from 27 league games was bettered only by Manchester City and Arsenal, a goal difference of plus-10 putting United behind those two, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Equally, momentum had turned. With a full pre-season to establish his ideas (rather than hone Ruben Amorim's), Carrick seems to have crafted a team who are less effective in attack and more porous in defense. The 4-4-2/4-2-4 in which his team line up out of position has been easily manipulated by superior teams and structural issues are not offset by intensity off the ball. United rank 15th for pressures applied and 10th for passes per defensive action, both measures of pressing applied by a team. Meanwhile, the attack has both been creating fewer chances -- the comeback against Villa notwithstanding -- and being more wasteful with them. It is a bad cocktail.

The risk would have been that United reaffirmed the commitment they made to Carrick after the three-goal defeats to Como and Bournemouth, one which always seemed to be conditioned on the imminent international break. Could anyone parachuted in at a moment's notice have done much better than four points against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa? The November international break has always functioned as a critical point for English clubs. Fail to pull the trigger now when there is time to get your feet under the desk and familiarize yourself with players -- who, for once, will have a few days back at the training ground after their commitments around the globe -- before the festive fixture list bears its teeth. In that context, sacking a relatively inexperienced coach like Carrick probably lessens the relegation risk somewhat.

Recent findings suggest that so, in principle, does hiring Pochettino. Here is a coach with over 400 games at the helm of English clubs, whose first job in the country with Southampton has afforded him some experience of the tight margins needed to avoid the drop zone. It was his work at Tottenham that so enamored Sir Alex Ferguson. Over five and a half years he forged Spurs into contenders for (but not winners of) the biggest prizes in the sport. Aggressive, attacking football with a young side imbued with English talent: everything except the silverware screams Manchester United in their pomp.

The price of that success was Pochettino's identity and Tottenham's intermingling. No bad thing when you are as successful as he was at first but it may have given the Argentine an expectation about his role in club football that he has brushed up against in subsequent jobs. At Chelsea he took umbrage at the hierarchy's insistence on affording him young signings rather than the veterans he wanted. The idea that set pieces should sit somewhat outside his jurisdiction and under "specialists" was not popular. At Tottenham, Pochettino had become accustomed to working cheek to jowl with executive chairman and part-owner Daniel Levy. Chelsea, like most Premier League clubs, have established numerous layers between the man in the dugout and the owners. He may not lose his rag in the manner of Antonio Conte but Pochettino is a deeply political operator. Any man who is not afraid to say what he sees could create a great deal of friction when he sees what has been going on at United these last few years.

Industry observers note that when he left Stamford Bridge the sense was that Pochettino was yesterday's man in the rapidly evolving world of the Premier League, even though in retrospect it appears he left strong foundations for Enzo Maresca to build on. That view was clearly not one that senior figures at United entirely discounted. After all, at the time they were seriously considering sacking Erik ten Hag after finishing eighth in the Premier League. Pochettino was among the names they considered before doubling down on the soon-to-be-deposed Dutchman.

Sources indicate that that was not the only time United could have got Pochettino. Indeed, when he left Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2022, he was interviewed before Ten Hag got the job. That was the most formal approach but there was also the restaurant summit with Ferguson at a Mayfair restaurant when Louis van Gaal was on the brink. And of course there was the chance to hire the 54-year-old in that window earlier this year when Carrick's interim spell was coming to an end and Pochettino had not yet recommitted to the USMNT.

It has been revealed that going for a coach they have consistently decided is not the best option for them will now cost them $10 million for his compensation plus the cost of his sizeable staff. The evidence of PSG, Chelsea and the USMNT is he can deliver to (realistic) expectations. In all likelihood things stabilize under Pochettino, the specter of relegation cast off. The scenario where he takes them down? It probably reflects yesterday's man taking a job at a club still enamored with an outdated vision of management. Pochettino is probably the most Ferguson-coded manager United have employed since the great man's anointed successor. His intense style of play will need willing participants and even if he finds them, it will also take time. That much was as apparent at the clubs where it clicked -- one win in his first seven league games with Southampton, three in nine at Spurs -- as it was elsewhere. Time is not a commodity a side in 18th place can really trade in.

According to recent reports, though Phil Neville was quite scathing in his assessment of Noussair Mazraoui, Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot on Sunday -- "that back four gets you relegated" -- in pure talent terms United should be absolutely fine. You can question how many players in the squad make up the core of the title-contending outfit they aspire to be but there has been plenty of decent business done buying decent players from decent Premier League teams. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, (in theory right now if not in practice) Youri Tielemans.

Recent findings suggest that getting another left back and another forward in January would solve a few issues created by more injury-addled players. Then again so would the players on the roster executing better. United rank fourth in the league for non-penalty xG but 11th for goals. Maybe that is because of their wayward finishing. Opta's shooting goals added metric, which assesses the likelihood of a goal being scored pre- and post-shot, ranks this team 17th in the league on -3.57. You wouldn't expect that to hold all season long, particularly when some of the worst offenders are Bruno Fernandes and Cunha. Of course, if it did, then yes, United would be in real trouble.

It has been revealed that the same at the other end. Yoro met a free kick with a fine header at Old Trafford on Sunday, drawing a springy save from a goalkeeper who could not stop the ball being turned in on the rebound. The slight issue is the goalkeeper was Senne Lammens and that was the fourth error leading to a goal that United have made this season. Low-volume statistics like these can occasionally betray you but in this case it speaks to a truth clear for all to see; the United defense is too slap-dashy. Young and old, players at Old Trafford have learned that basic errors rarely lead to lasting consequences. If this clumsiness continues -- and it should not be treated as a given that it does -- then the crisis could deepen.

According to recent reports, it's worth saying from the off that if you're rooting for chaos you'd want to see Manchester United's numbers trend down quite dramatically for there to be much in the analytics that indicates 18th or worse. The "best" relegated sides of recent years are probably Leicester City in 2022-23, sent down to the Championship on 34 points and -0.39 non-penalty xG difference (npxGD) per game, and West Ham three years later. They slipped through the trap door on 39 points and -0.26 npxGD, just a shade worse than Tottenham. Manchester United have sunk to levels below that in past seasons but not this.

Right now there is a long way to go to catch up with the worst teams in the league so far. Ipswich Town have accrued points and look to be a hard out but they are averaging -0.67 npxG difference per game. They are the worst of the newly promoted sides but both Hull City (-0.5) and Coventry City (-0.48) are delivering worrying analytics. The former have the advantage of those points they accrued early in the season and Hull deserve credit for how sparky and organized they are given the talent deficit Sergej Jakirovic is working with. Apply some of those principles with United's talent and competence is no longer the limit.

It isn't just the promoted sides that look bad. Sunderland have a case of difficult second-season syndrome. The best that can be stated for Newcastle is that, like Hull, they've banked some fortuitous points. We can maybe ignore Aston Villa given how rarely their xG reflects the results Unai Emery gets.

Then there is Crystal Palace and, well, yikes. In the six seasons before this one only seven teams have had a worse npxGD per game than Palace's -0.86, which is a true marker of inadequacy. These levels Pierre Sage has plummeted the Conference League winners to aren't much better than Norwich City in 2021-22, Luton Town in 2023-24 or the carnival of ineptitude that was Leicester and Southampton two years ago. Palace are bad. So, so bad.

At least they are in results terms. The talent doesn't seem that bad even if the drip-drip of departures over the last year -- Oliver Glasner, Maxence Lacroix, Marc Guehi, Eberechi Eze -- has lowered their ceiling. With a Thomas Frank in charge you could see them move back on the right path promptly. Maybe the northeast triumvirate swing upwards too. Suddenly then there might be a space opening up for a team that is both bad and unlucky. That is, of course, assuming that there are three spots opened up for relegated teams this season.

In a recent development, of course Manchester City might yet have a spot in next season's Championship with their name on it. City were found to have breached 114 of the Premier League's rules by an independent commission, a verdict they are in the midst of appealing.

Industry observers note that separate to the process of establishing whether the commission erred in its duties is the matter of sanctioning City. That will be decided by the same three-person panel though it is not yet clear when the hearing will take place nor what the Premier League will expect. Given the abrasive language used by the league about one of its member clubs, it is hard to see them settling for a proposal that does not end with City out of the top flight at the end of the season.

The Premier League wants this process wrapped up comprehensively but swiftly. Much of the football world expects City to get hit hard, hence why bookmakers have Enzo Maresca's side among the three most likely teams to be relegated. A sweeping points deduction at the Etihad Stadium would be greeted with delight around Old Trafford for many reasons. The fact that it might insulate United from their own mismanagement is certainly one of them.

There are, however, no guarantees that this process will reach its conclusion before the end of the season. City could endure, dragging out a process they have made plain they believe to be compromised at its most basic principles. Can they keep the wheels spinning for another seven-plus months? Or argue their way to the sort of punishment that does not send them off the edge of the Premier League map? It may be hard to do but it is the sort of unlikely event that, for the time being, might be required to send United to the Championship.

The video assistant referee did their own check and stuck with the decision before Calvert-Lewin calmly sent Emiliano Martinez the wrong way from the spot. As soon as Rogers realised VAR's verdict to uphold Oliver's decision, he reacted in disbelief, "That's the worst decision I've ever seen.".

Recent findings suggest that chelsea's defeat means they now sit eighth in the table, with five wins and as many defeats. Alonso's start hasn't lived up to expectations and the latest setback has raised doubts over his ability to turn the tide at Stamford Bridge.

Former Premier League referee Mike Dean felt Oliver got the decision spot on when speaking on Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday. He said he thought it was "the right call" because "the distance is quite far when Bogle strikes it to where Rogers is.".

According to recent reports, dean added: "But I think he does direct it away from goal. It's probably inconclusive when you see the pictures, but it's not a wrong decision by the referee on the field. He's made the call. VAR will never overturn that kind of decision.".

This is the second consecutive game a contentious decision has played a role in a Chelsea defeat. Huge debate ensued when Brian Brobbey went down after a challenge from Levi Colwill and won the winning penalty for Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Industry observers note that alonso opted not to blame the 1-0 defeat on that controversial call and instead pointed the finger at his team's defending. He may well take the same approach in response to yet another miserable defensive display from his side, who have conceded 19 goals in 11 games.

Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.
  • For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.
  • Sources indicate that in late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

Sources indicate that in late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AIIB emphasized that not every matter needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank said in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it noted.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts.".

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," mentioned Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

Recent findings suggest that she argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

Industry observers note that the AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it said, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Industry observers note that urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

For 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

"The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly important documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement aims, vary widely or are missing entirely," noted Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond promptly and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, stated the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough.".

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he said, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

Criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not fresh. A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

According to recent reports, the AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

Recent findings suggest that for Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she stated.

It has been revealed that as of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

Recent findings suggest that but Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles.".

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive.".

The new rules have been in effect for only 10 months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Steinert stated fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

Such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert noted. However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank said that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns.".

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat said Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

Hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards.".

This article was originally written in German.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Fiorentina coach gave his pre-match press conference at the Viola Park ahead of the trip to the U-Power Stadium, where kick-off is at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT].

Sources indicate that “Ndour has been training separately and will join the group tomorrow. “He’s an crucial player and I’m happy to have him back, but he’s been out for a long time, so his minutes will increase gradually.”.

Vanoli also responded to reports that he might free Franco Mastantuono from defensive duties.

Sources indicate that “I’m sorry you’re spreading the idea that an attacker has to stay close to goal. That’s your speculation. Kvara said that if he didn’t defend, he didn’t play. Industry observers note that the shirt itself is a faithful reproduction of the original design, featuring the signature red base with faint striping, white sleeves, the JVC sponsor and a centralised club crest. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4986 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane remarked as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.
  • In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre.
  • Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane remarked as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he noted of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”.

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”.

According to recent reports, so much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Industry observers note that kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and stated: “You held it together. You got through it.” It highlighted how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Industry observers note that kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

In a recent development, kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg.

In a recent development, for his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

According to recent reports, both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he stated. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

It has been revealed that kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

Recent findings suggest that and he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

In a recent development, that work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany remarked: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”.

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has revealed Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before promptly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

In a recent development, the choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Recent findings suggest that selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:24 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

According to recent reports, tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

With Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

Their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

In a recent development, villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

It has been revealed that they will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how rapidly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

It has been revealed that true, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the Final through injury.

Still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

It has been revealed that emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of fresh players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

Recent findings suggest that ‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely important but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

Sources indicate that A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

It has been revealed that on this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with Mauricio Pochettino looking like he is on the way to Manchester United, there could be a major vacancy to fill for the U.S. men's national team with the head coach position. With a newly introduced national training center, an established team, and young players coming up from everywhere to push that squad, it's a job that should be an attractive one to managers around the world, depending on the direction that U.S. Soccer wants to go.

Pochettino was an appropriate splash hire ahead of the World Cup, and it's not surprising that a top team in the world still wanted him. But when looking to build a stable base for 2030, there's a chance that the powers that be would prefer a candidate who would be more bought into American soccer, so when looking at potential candidates to take the role, it makes sense to sound out both options, and here's the list it has come to:.

The best American coach in Major League Soccer and someone who also got my vote for Coach of the Year after leading Nashville SC to a league-record 77 points in the regular season, B.J. Callaghan will need to be among the top contenders for the USMNT job if the U.S. Soccer Federation chooses to go with an American fit instead of another splash hire like Pochettino. He already has experience coaching and leading the USMNT during tournament play, leading the squad to the 2023 Concacaf Nations League title before heading to Nashville and turning them into one of the most complete sides in MLS. Callaghan has paid his dues, going from the college ranks all the way to the professional ones, and is someone with intimate knowledge of the American soccer system. If looking to go in a more traditional direction while also not shifting the vision of Olympic play, Callaghan is a solid choice.

While Nancy's time at Celtic after leaving the Columbus Crew was a moment to forget, not all of that was his fault, as the French manager has done nothing but succeed in his career, no matter where he has gone. Limit his resources, and he'll develop a system to get the best out of what he has; increase them, and he'll go toe to toe with everyone, and that flexibility is critical in international play. It's rare that you have your first-choice 11 available, and being able to work around that is what can make a difference on the margins. Nancy could want to still test himself in Europe but it doesn't hurt to call.

Right now overseeing the U-23s, the former Los Angeles FC manager would likely be in the USMNT succession blueprint for Pochettino. The goal was to bring both camps together as much as possible and ensure that they had a similar style, as plenty of players would go between both squads depending on needs. The issue is that this has all happened faster than anyone would've anticipated, since if Steve Cherundolo was going to take over the USMNT, that'd likely be a 2028 post-Olympic deal rather than right at this moment. But also looking at the performance of LAFC without Cherundolo, it's clear that he held things together plenty in that squad and that he could be a fit for the role; the question is just when.

According to recent reports, you have to make the call, and it looks like they will. We all know what the answer likely is, but if there's an opening and the USMNT wants the best manager available, Pep Guardiola is right there. The former Manchester City, Bayern Munich and Barcelona boss is expected to be their top target, according to The Athletic.

Recent findings suggest that they reportedly called Jurgen Klopp before hiring Pochettino, and this would be a similar scenario as Klopp is now with Germany. Guardiola isn't going to stay out of management forever, so why not try to bring him back in on the road to 2030? He would be facing similar problems to Pochettino of not knowing if he'll be a long-term fit for the role, but those aren't things that should come into play if the goal is to hire the best available manager who is a fit for the job.

A name that came up after the World Cup when decisions were being made on whether Pochettino should be extended, Roberto Martinez could come into consideration yet again. On paper, he offers a mix of European experience and the staying power of someone who has overseen multiple international sides for an entire cycle, but it's tough to say he'd be a good fit. Martinez wasn't able to lead Belgium's golden generation to a title and struggled to get Portugal to play to their talent as well. With a USMNT that have the world at their feet as young players begin to lead the way, it'd be better to go the domestic route before turning to Martinez.

Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration.
  • According to recent reports, every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter.
  • According to recent reports, speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate newly introduced arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems?

According to recent reports, every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter. Since last year, that role has been held by Natalie Pawlik, a parliamentary representative from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD).

According to recent reports, speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed. They rightly expect that people who live in Germany permanently will learn our language and abide by our laws.".

The Commissioner for Integration is part of the Federal Ministry of Labor because ensuring that newcomers find work quickly is especially notable.

According to recent reports, the integration reportwas created by a team led by Frank Kalter, director of the German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM), drawing on official government statistics, surveys and independent studies. They found that when all immigrant groups are counted, about 30% of the population today has some sort of migration background — even if that comes down to only one parent.

Pawlik commented: "This is an notable message at a time when the discussion often focuses primarily on problems related to supposedly failed integration." Kalter also pointed out that the employment rate among immigrants in Germany is higher than in most other EU countries — nearly 70%.

In a recent development, and they work primarily in one sector: "In recent years, the biggest increase of workers without German citizenship has been in the health and social services sector." According to the data, there were about 1.8 million people without a German passport working in Germany in 2009. By 2025, this number had more than tripled to 5.8 million.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

However, problems remain. In nearly all immigrant groups, women have difficulty finding employment, especially if they have children and their husbands are employed. Only about 60% of women in such families are employed, whereas nearly 88% of women in families with German passports are employed.

There are also immigrant groups that face barriers to accessing educational opportunities and the job market. These are mostly young men who came to Germany as refugees. And if one considers citizenship as a distinguishing factor, the percentage of convicted criminals who are not German citizens is far higher — around 40% — than their share of the population. And they are also reported to the police far more frequently. At the same time, individuals without a German passport are also more likely to become victims of crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that pawlik emphasizes that language acquisition is the foundation and starting point of any successful integration. But this is precisely where the government tightened its purse strings earlier this year to save money. Many integration courses are now no longer offered at all or receive less government funding. Pawlik made it clear that she is strongly critical of these cuts, even though she herself is part of the federal government.

Most recently, Pawlik and her fellow Social Democrats have been advocating for people who have been working in Germany for some time to receive more secure residency permits — especially those from Syria and Ukraine. On Tuesday, SPD lawmakers adopted a position paper on the matter. In the paper, they propose that existing legal rights that allow workers to remain in the country should also apply to refugees. In other words, it would give working refugees a more secure status.

But will the conservatives from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) — who lead the coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) — support this? "You'll have to ask the interior minister," Pawlik replied when asked by DW. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is known for being a hardliner on immigration policy.

This article was originally published in German.

Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later.
  • Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.
  • Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”.

Sources indicate that this was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM.

It has been revealed that the precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

In a recent development, so while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

Industry observers note that the anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

According to recent reports, arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”.

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Sources indicate that aside from their stadium being called Highbury, Fleetwood Town’s red shirts with white sleeves also bear a striking resemblance to Arsenal’s home kit. The club in its current guise was founded in 1997, although previous iterations date back to 1908 under the name Fleetwood FC.

There is no evidence or anecdote suggesting Arsenal were the inspiration, so it appears the kit clash is a coincidence. Arsenal will be wearing their navy away strip.

The club’s most famous son is surely Jamie Vardy, who scored 31 goals in 36 appearances for Fleetwood in the 2011-12 season before Leicester City made their move.

An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”.

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Recent findings suggest that arteta remarked: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”Full team news on the way shortly.

Arsenal are reportedly the latest club to show an interest in Tornike Kvaratskhelia, the younger brother of Paris Saint-Germain superstar Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

The highly-rated 16-year-old has previously also been mentioned as a target for Manchester United and Liverpool.

Now a new upgrade from TEAMtalk has emerged stating that Arsenal are also in the race, along with other Premier League clubs such as Manchester City, Brighton, and Aston Villa.

Kvaratskhelia looks like another exciting young talent who could go on to have similar potential to his older brother, who emerged from relative obscurity before taking Serie A by storm during his time at Napoli.

That earned the Georgia international a massive move to PSG and he’s continued to shine there, winning the Champions League twice with the Ligue 1 giants.

Arsenal could be set to sign another Georgian youngster if they land Kvaratskhelia’s brother, following similar recent business.

BBC Sport reported on the Gunners pursuing Andria Bartishvili in what could end up being a smart purchase for the future.

Kvaratskhelia and Bartishvili could be key to ensuring Arteta still has another generation of top Arsenal players coming through once this current squad has peaked.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Aquile will spend at least another week on top of the Serie A table following today’s 3-0 victory over Cagliari at the Stadio Olimpico.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, gennaro Gattuso expressed his ‘pride’ as Lazio swept Lecce aside 3-0 to stay top of the Serie A table. ‘I don’t mind misplaced passes, because we play at such a high tempo.’.

The Aquile will spend at least another week on top of the Serie A table following today’s 3-0 victory over Cagliari at the Stadio Olimpico.

Tijjani Noslin found the net twice before Davide Frattesi put the cherry on top with a delightful lob in the final minutes of the match.

“I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown by the team today,” Gattuso told DAZN Italia.

According to recent reports, “We didn’t have the best start, but then got control of the game, both in possession and off the ball. Lecce are an uncomfortable opponent, they always come and push you, so it is fundamental for us to keep this attitude.”.

There is always some concern for coaches after the break for international duty, but Gattuso assures he had no such qualms about his Lazio players.

“I saw the way they were training, so I was not worried. There is a great spirit and application, we’ve got to keep going like this. It is all down to the players, they are putting in the right mentality, hunger and sense of belonging. They are doing something incredible.”.

Lazio are top of the table and still unbeaten in Serie A despite a lot of injury problems, as today they were missing Mattia Zaccagni, Nuno Tavares, Josip Sutalo and Adam Marusic.

Nicolò Rovella also came off the bench late on and is still trying to work his way back to full fitness after numerous challenges.

“Rovella can give us more vertical passes, as when he gets the ball, he immediately looks up and forward,” explained the coach.

According to recent reports, “I think we also need to talk about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru. He deserves more. We’ve got to give Rovella playing time so that he can regain fitness, then he can give us an vital hand.”.

Considering how well Lazio are doing under Gattuso so far this season, is there anything he still hasn’t seen and wants them to improve?

“I don’t mind losing the ball with misplaced passes that much, because when you play at a high tempo, that can happen. I am more interested in the mentality of the side and how they are hanging in there under pressure.

“I am satisfied, you always want something more, but at this tempo there are going to be some misplaced passes. We can improve our reading of the game, as for example today when we struggled to get through the middle, we needed to spread the game out wide.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

Despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

It has been revealed that the outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

Industry observers note that it’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t promptly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

It has been revealed that on Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

In a recent development, saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Recent findings suggest that kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Sources indicate that tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

According to recent reports, saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

It has been revealed that yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor indicated him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

It has been revealed that O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager revealed up well.

#37135. Breaking: Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle
